title: Store events carry no secret material
asA: operator who ships store event logs to a third-party observability provider
iWant: every field on every store event to be limited to store metadata; no domain data, no credential material, no secret values
soThat: a log-store breach is not a domain-data breach and the ops team does not have to negotiate a redaction rule with the provider

acceptanceCriteria.description: The fields on the opened, migrated, backupCheckpoint, and closed events are restricted to store metadata: event name, ISO-8601 timestamp, store identifier, schema version integers, migration version integers, migration description strings, and backup artifact paths. No event field carries a value read from a domain row.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the store is taken through open, migrate, backup, and close
acceptanceCriteria.when: every event record captured on the sink is inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: every field on every record matches one of the metadata field types listed above, and no field's value equals a value read from any domain table

acceptanceCriteria.description: A grep of the store facade source for domain-table column names, secret-flagged column names, and the values of well-known secret columns (session handles, token secrets, private keys) finds them referenced only inside the narrow CRUD verbs that read or write those columns, never inside the event-emission call sites.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the store facade source and the domain schema definition
acceptanceCriteria.then: matches appear only inside CRUD verb bodies and never inside onEvent call arguments or event-record construction sites
